newsitem.title: USA: International Paper to sell land rights.
newsitem.headline: International Paper to sell land rights.

text.p: International Paper said on Monday that it had agreed to sell the management rights for 175,000 acres of timberland in Western Pennsylvania and New York as part of an effort to raise $1 billion through selling off assets.
Also slated for sale, the company said in a statment, were several businesses within its decorative products division and its InterSpun business, which is part of the company's Veratec division.
International Paper, a producer of packaging, paper and building material, added that it will close a production line at a Masonite manufacturing facility in Pennsylvania.
Company Chief Executive John Dillon said the sales would allow the company to focus resources on businesses where International Paper holds leadership positions.

The timberland management rights sale, made to Forest Investment Associates, will be completed within 12 to 18 months, the company said, with the first of five land deal transactions closing next month.
International Paper said proceeds from the first transaction will come to roughly $40 million and total proceeds from the rights sale is estimated at up to $200 million.

"All of the actions announced today are expected to be completed within a year and were anticipated in the company's July 8 announcement of a $535-million reserve against second quarter earnings and a 9,000 reduction in International Paper's workforce," the company said.
